CHRONOLOGICAL FULL THREAD:

[1] 11 Aug 2026 13:11 UTC -- James Salas Guillen -> Kevin Lelitte, cc Simon Burford. Subject: "Cority - Applicant Data Import file".
Hi Kevin and Simon,

I wanted to provide an update on the Cority Applicant Data Import.

Following several uploads/imports in Production with real data, we've identified several formatting issues in the source report that require manual clean-up before the file can be successfully uploaded. These issues were not apparent during earlier testing and only became evident once we started processing production data.

The current report requires the following manual amendments before it can be uploaded to Cority:
1. Remove quotation marks from all fields (e.g. "First Name of Employee").
2. Ensure all column headers are contained within a single header row. Currently, the headers split across multiple rows when converted to CSV.
3. Format the Date of Birth field as a date only (dd/mm/yyyy) with no time component.
4. Ensure the file contains all 27 expected columns and corresponding headers even if no data is available.

Ideally, if the above changes can be implemented within the report itself, the report should be exported directly to CSV rather than Excel to eliminate the additional conversion and clean-up steps currently required.

As previously discussed, there may be an opportunity to implement these changes directly within the PXD reporting module, which would remove the need for ongoing manual work.

In addition, I have identified what appears to be a potential mismatch in the column mapping between our report and Cority. I currently have a support ticket open with the Cority support team to investigate this further. If the issue turns out to be on our side, we may also need to adjust the report column order accordingly.

Would it be possible to review whether these report changes can be made within PXD (RECSUP20_Applicant Cority Interface File)? Making these amendments at source would significantly reduce the manual effort required each time the file is processed for import.

Best wishes,
James Salas, Senior Functional Analyst, HR Systems | People Department | University of Oxford

[2] 18 Aug 2026 11:55 UTC -- Simon Burford replies (RE:).
Hi James,

I'm sure this is possible to do.

However, when I save the report as CSV and open it in notepad++ I see the following: [embedded screenshot -- see "Attachment note" below; the column headers to me look like they are in one row already, so how are you currently getting/viewing the CSV where it's split over multiple rows?]

Quotation marks in this file only exist where there is a comma in the data field, to prevent the columns breaking (e.g. in the screenshot above the division name "MATHS, PHYSICAL & LIFE SCIENCES" has a comma in it, so it adds quotes to stop the file interpreting MATHS as one column and PHYSICAL & LIFE SCIENCES as the next column). I'm assuming that this is expected behaviour and Cority can handle this?

The date of birth field is clearly an issue so this can hopefully be sorted, the headers are just the names of the text boxes but I have an idea of how this could be fixed so fingers crossed, but it definitely has commas denoting the columns even if the data is blank, so that should be fine.

Many thanks,
Simon Burford, HR Systems Analysis and Insights Manager, HR Systems | People Department | University of Oxford
